English: Dirt Patch
A makeshift patch of earth, roughly cleared for the first games. Marked by trampled ground and wooden stakes, it draws the clan together in simple contests.
Stone Boundary
Rough stones outline the court, discouraging wandering livestock and giving the games structure. The first sign of permanent effort, it fosters a sense of territory.
Raised Platform
Low earthen platforms border the court, elevating the field of play and suggesting the beginnings of ceremonial purpose.
Marker Ring
Stone rings, hoisted on posts, serve as goals and markers for the sacred ballgame, attracting greater crowds and inspiring awe.
Spectator Stand
Timber and stone benches rise above the court, allowing the clans people to gather and witness the games, promoting unity and shared tradition.
Scorers Pavilion
A dedicated structure for officials to record and judge the games, encouraging fairness and fostering clan prestige.
Chieftains Seat
A prominent throne constructed for the clan leader, symbolizing authority and cementing the courts role as a center of unity.
Ceremonial Court
The court becomes a place of ritual, with altars and decorative carvings. Festivals and games now unite the whole clan, inspiring loyalty and awe.
High Arena
Massive stepped terraces and ceremonial entryways surround the court. The arena dominates the region, gathering crowds from afar and enhancing the clans prestige.
Grand Mesoamerican Ballcourt
A vast, monumental court with sculpted walls, ceremonial plazas, and sacred rings. The heart of the clan, it is a beacon of unity and tradition for all who witness it.
